I now have a complete picture of the repository. Here is my thorough report:

---

## Repository Overview: `/Users/tim/dokuwiki-docker`

### Purpose

This is a **Dockerized DokuWiki** project -- a simple, self-contained Docker image for running [DokuWiki](https://www.dokuwiki.org/), a popular open-source wiki application. The image is based on `php:apache` and packages DokuWiki for easy container deployment. The GitHub image is published as `ununseptium/dokuwiki-docker` (also referenced as `nevotheless/dokuwiki-docker` in the Trivy workflow).

**License:** MIT (Copyright 2016)

**Git remote:** `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/nevotheless/dokuwiki-docker` (routed through Entire.io)

**Branches:** `master` (current), `entire/checkpoints/v1`
**Tags:** `7.3`

---

### Complete File Tree (excluding `.git/`, `.entire/`, `.opencode/node_modules/`)

```
.
├── .entire/
│   ├── .gitignore
│   └── settings.json
├── .github/
│   ├── ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md
│   └── workflows/
│       ├── dockerpublish.yml
│       └── trivy.yml
├── .opencode/
│   ├── .gitignore
│   ├── package.json
│   └── package-lock.json
├── Dockerfile
├── docker-compose.yml
├── hello-entire.md
├── LICENSE
└── README.md
```

---

### Full Content of Every Key File

#### 1. `Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
FROM php:apache

LABEL maintainer tim@arctium.io

# Download dokuwiki source
RUN curl -O https://download.dokuwiki.org/src/dokuwiki/dokuwiki-stable.tgz

# Install unzip and extract the dokuwiki files to the actual webserver folder
RUN apt-get update \
    && tar -xzvf dokuwiki-stable.tgz --strip-components=1 -C /var/www/html \
    && cd /var/www/html \
    && find . -type d -exec chmod 755 {} \; \
    && find . -type f -exec chmod 644 {} \; \
    && chown -R www-data:www-data .
```

**Key observations:**
- Base image: `php:apache` (untagged -- always pulls the latest `php:apache` image, which is currently PHP 8.x with Debian Bookworm)
- Downloads `dokuwiki-stable.tgz` from the official DokuWiki download server -- this means it always fetches the **latest stable release** at build time (no version pinning)
- Extracts directly into `/var/www/html` (Apache's default document root)
- Sets permissions: directories to 755, files to 644, owned by `www-data`
- The comment mentions "Install unzip" but no `apt-get install unzip` is actually present -- the extraction uses `tar` instead
- No `.dockerignore` file exists
- No health check defined
- No PHP extensions explicitly installed (relies on whatever the base `php:apache` image provides)

#### 2. `docker-compose.yml`

```yaml
# Example docker-compose file
version: '3'
services:
  dokuwiki:
    image: 'ununseptium/dokuwiki-docker'
    ports:
      - '80:80'
      - '443:443'
    volumes:
      - 'data:/var/www/html'
volumes:
  data:
    driver: local
```

**Key observations:**
- Uses the pre-built image `ununseptium/dokuwiki-docker` (not building from local Dockerfile)
- Exposes both HTTP (80) and HTTPS (443), though the image itself does not configure SSL
- Mounts a named volume `data` to `/var/www/html` -- this means the wiki data persists across container restarts
- Note: Using `version: '3'` is now deprecated in modern Docker Compose
- Uses the legacy `driver: local` specification (unnecessary since `local` is the default)

#### 3. `README.md`

```markdown
[![](https://images.microbadger.com/badges/image/ununseptium/dokuwiki-docker.svg)](https://microbadger.com/images/ununseptium/dokuwiki-docker "Get your own image badge on microbadger.com")

# dokuwiki-docker
Simple to use and highly versatile open-source wiki... conveniently packaged as a container image

> This Dockerfile contains a streamlined and not blown-up approach to run a dockerized version of dokuwiki. 
> It's based on the php:7.x-apache image which ships with apache and php7 right out of the box.

## How-to use this

Instead of just starting the image, you should consider using a docker-compose file to spin up your services. The example file will attach a persistent volume to your dokuwiki service and make sure the needed ports are openened.

    # Example docker-compose file
    version: '3'
    services:
      dokuwiki:
        image: 'ununseptium/dokuwiki-docker'
        ports:
          - '80:80'
          - '443:443'
        volumes:
          - 'data:/var/www/html'
    volumes:
      data:
        driver: local

Once you either navigated to the cloned repo or created the file by yourself, you can use these commands:

**Start the Service via**

`docker-compose up`

**Tear down the Service via**

`docker-compose down`
```

**Key observations:**
- The README references `php:7.x-apache` but the Dockerfile now uses `php:apache` (the README is outdated)
- Uses microbadger.com for image size badges (microbadger.com has been shut down)
- Simple usage instructions only

#### 4. `.github/workflows/dockerpublish.yml`

```yaml
name: Docker

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
    tags:
      - v*
  pull_request:

env:
  IMAGE_NAME: dokuwiki-docker

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Run tests
        run: |
          if [ -f docker-compose.test.yml ]; then
            docker-compose --file docker-compose.test.yml build
            docker-compose --file docker-compose.test.yml run sut
          else
            docker build . --file Dockerfile
          fi

  push:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Build image
        run: docker build . --file Dockerfile --tag $IMAGE_NAME
      - name: Log into registry
        run: echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" | docker login docker.pkg.github.com -u ${{ github.actor }} --password-stdin
      - name: Push image
        run: |
          IMAGE_ID=docker.pkg.github.com/${{ github.repository }}/$IMAGE_NAME
          IMAGE_ID=$(echo $IMAGE_ID | tr '[A-Z]' '[a-z]')
          VERSION=$(echo "${{ github.ref }}" | sed -e 's,.*/\(.*\),\1,')
          [[ "${{ github.ref }}" == "refs/tags/"* ]] && VERSION=$(echo $VERSION | sed -e 's/^v//')
          [ "$VERSION" == "master" ] && VERSION=latest
          echo IMAGE_ID=$IMAGE_ID
          echo VERSION=$VERSION
          docker tag dokuwiki-docker $IMAGE_ID:$VERSION
          docker push $IMAGE_ID:$VERSION
```

**Key observations:**
- Uses `actions/checkout@v2` (outdated, current is v4)
- Pushes to **GitHub Packages** (docker.pkg.github.com) -- this is the legacy GitHub Packages Docker registry, now deprecated in favor of `ghcr.io`
- Publishes `master` as `latest`, and `v*` tags with the version stripped
- Tests by simply building the Dockerfile (no actual application tests)
- Uses the legacy `docker-compose` (v1) command syntax

#### 5. `.github/workflows/trivy.yml`

```yaml
name: build

on:
  push:
    branches: [ master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ master ]
  schedule:
    - cron: '15 22 * * *'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    name: Build
    runs-on: "ubuntu-18.04"
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Build an image from Dockerfile
        run: |
          docker build -t nevotheless/dokuwiki-docker:${{ github.sha }} .

      - name: Run Trivy vulnerability scanner
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@2a2157eb22c08c9a1fac99263430307b8d1bc7a2
        with:
          image-ref: 'nevotheless/dokuwiki-docker:${{ github.sha }}'
          format: 'template'
          template: '@/contrib/sarif.tpl'
          output: 'trivy-results.sarif'
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'

      - name: Upload Trivy scan results to GitHub Security tab
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2
        with:
          sarif_file: 'trivy-results.sarif'
```

**Key observations:**
- Runs Trivy vulnerability scanning on every push/PR to master, plus a **daily schedule** (`cron: '15 22 * * *'`)
- Uses `ubuntu-18.04` runner (EOL -- no longer available on GitHub Actions)
- Pins Trivy action by commit SHA: `2a2157eb22c08c9a1fac99263430307b8d1bc7a2`
- Scans for CRITICAL and HIGH severity vulnerabilities
- Uploads results as SARIF to GitHub Security tab
- Uses a different image name (`nevotheless/dokuwiki-docker`) than the publish workflow (`ununseptium/dokuwiki-docker`)

#### 6. `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md`

```markdown
<!--

PLEASE ONLY REPORT APPLICATION SPECIFIC ISSUES HERE.
FOR MORE GENERAL ISSUES PLEASE HEAD OVER TO THE 
META REPOSITORY ununseptium/dockerize
https://github.com/ununseptium/dockerize/issues

-->

**Description**

**Output of `docker version`:**

**Output of `docker info`:**

**Steps to reproduce:**
 1. 
 2. 
 3. 

**Additional informations**
```

#### 7. `LICENSE`

Standard MIT License, Copyright (c) 2016 (no specific name listed).

#### 8. `hello-entire.md`

```markdown
# Hello Entire

This repo is my first Entire checkpoint demo.
```

A demo/test file for the Entire.io checkpoint system.

#### 9. `.opencode/package.json`

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@opencode-ai/plugin": "1.17.15"
  }
}
```

Internal tooling for the OpenCode AI plugin.

#### 10. `.entire/settings.json`

```json
{
  "enabled": true
}
```

Entire.io checkpoint system is enabled for this repo.

---

### Version Summary

| Component | Version | Pinning |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| **Base image** | `php:apache` (untagged) | **None** -- always pulls latest (currently PHP 8.x on Debian Bookworm) |
| **PHP** | Whatever `php:apache` ships (8.x) | **None** -- floating tag |
| **Web server** | Apache (bundled in `php:apache`) | **None** |
| **DokuWiki** | `dokuwiki-stable.tgz` | **None** -- always downloads latest stable at build time |
| **Docker Compose format** | Version 3 | N/A |
| **Trivy Action** | Pinned by SHA | `2a2157eb22c08c9a1fac99263430307b8d1bc7a2` |
| **GitHub Actions checkout** | v2 (publish) / v3 (trivy) | Major version tags |
| **OpenCode plugin** | `@opencode-ai/plugin` 1.17.15 | Exact version |

---

### Notable Issues and Observations

1. **No version pinning whatsoever** for the core stack -- neither the PHP base image nor DokuWiki itself are pinned to specific versions. Every `docker build` pulls the latest of everything, making builds non-reproducible.

2. **Outdated CI/CD:**
   - `ubuntu-18.04` runner in the Trivy workflow is no longer available on GitHub Actions
   - `actions/checkout@v2` is outdated (current: v4)
   - GitHub Packages Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`) is deprecated in favor of `ghcr.io`
   - `docker-compose` v1 command syntax (v2 uses `docker compose` without hyphen)

3. **No `.dockerignore`** file -- the `.git/`, `.entire/`, `.opencode/`, and other unnecessary directories would be included in the Docker build context.

4. **No health check** in the Dockerfile.

5. **Inconsistent image naming** between workflows (`ununseptium/dokuwiki-docker` vs `nevotheless/dokuwiki-docker`).

6. **No SSL configuration** despite exposing port 443.

7. **README is outdated** -- references `php:7.x-apache` while the Dockerfile uses `php:apache`.

8. **The `apt-get update` runs** but no packages are installed (the comment mentions "Install unzip" but only `tar` is used for extraction).

Now I have a complete picture. Here's the analysis:

---

## Repository Health Report: `dokuwiki-docker`

### Overall Status: Significantly Outdated

The last meaningful code change was the shift from `php:7.3-apache` to `php:apache` (tag `7.3`), and the CI/CD hasn't been updated since ~2022. This repo has **4+ years of accumulated technical debt**.

---

### 1. Dockerfile (`Dockerfile`)

| Issue | Severity | Details |
|-------|----------|---------|
| No base image version pin | High | `php:apache` floats to latest (currently PHP 8.5). Builds are non-reproducible. |
| No DokuWiki version pin | High | Downloads `dokuwiki-stable.tgz` -- always latest at build time. Current stable is **2025-05-14 "Librarian"**. |
| No `.dockerignore` | Medium | `.git/`, `.entire/`, `.opencode/` all leak into build context. |
| No `HEALTHCHECK` | Low | No container health probe defined. |
| Stale comment | Low | Says "Install unzip" but uses `tar`. Misleading. |
| No PHP extensions installed | Medium | DokuWiki may need extensions like `gd`, `intl`, `mbstring` -- none explicitly installed. |

### 2. Docker Compose (`docker-compose.yml`)

| Issue | Severity | Details |
|-------|----------|---------|
| `version: '3'` deprecated | Low | Compose V2 ignores this field; it's noise. |
| `driver: local` unnecessary | Low | `local` is the default volume driver. |
| No build context | Low | Only references pre-built image, can't build locally. |

### 3. GitHub Actions - Publish (`dockerpublish.yml`)

| Issue | Severity | Details |
|-------|----------|---------|
| **`actions/checkout@v2`** | High | Current is **v4**. v2 uses deprecated Node.js 12 runtime. |
| **Legacy Docker registry** | Critical | Pushes to `docker.pkg.github.com` which was **shut down Feb 2025**. Must migrate to `ghcr.io`. |
| `docker-compose` v1 syntax | Medium | Should use `docker compose` (v2, no hyphen). |
| `docker.pkg.github.com` login | Critical | Login command targets a dead registry. |

### 4. GitHub Actions - Trivy Scan (`trivy.yml`)

| Issue | Severity | Details |
|-------|----------|---------|
| **`ubuntu-18.04` runner** | Critical | **Removed from GitHub Actions in April 2023**. This workflow is completely broken. |
| `actions/checkout@v3` | High | Current is **v4**. |
| **Pinned Trivy SHA** | High | `2a2157eb...` is very old. Current action is much newer. |
| `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2` | Medium | Current is **v3**. |
| Inconsistent image name | Medium | Uses `nevotheless/dokuwiki-docker` vs `ununseptium/dokuwiki-docker` in the publish workflow. |

### 5. README (`README.md`)

| Issue | Severity | Details |
|-------|----------|---------|
| References `php:7.x-apache` | Medium | Dockerfile uses `php:apache` (PHP 8.x). |
| Microbadger badge | Medium | microbadger.com is effectively defunct. Should use shields.io or ghcr.io badges. |
| `docker-compose` command | Low | Should reference `docker compose` (v2). |

---

### What Needs to Be Done

**Priority 1 - Broken (must fix):**
1. **Migrate CI publish workflow to `ghcr.io`** -- the old Docker registry is dead
2. **Fix Trivy workflow** -- change `ubuntu-18.04` to `ubuntu-latest`
3. **Update action versions** -- `actions/checkout@v4`, `github/codeql-action@v3`

**Priority 2 - Outdated (should fix):**
4. **Pin the base image** -- e.g. `php:8.4-apache` for stability
5. **Pin DokuWiki version** -- e.g. `dokuwiki-2025-05-14.tgz` or use a build arg
6. **Add required PHP extensions** -- `gd`, `intl`, `mbstring` at minimum
7. **Add `.dockerignore`** file
8. **Update Trivy action** to latest version

**Priority 3 - Nice to have:**
9. Remove deprecated `version: '3'` from compose file
10. Add `HEALTHCHECK` to Dockerfile
11. Fix README to match current state
12. Add `docker compose` (v2) instructions
13. Clean up misleading comments in Dockerfile

  - `gd` braucht auf Debian: `libpng-dev`, `libjpeg-dev`, `libfreetype6-dev`
  - `opcache` ist ein Core-Extension, muss nur aktiviert werden
- `docker-php-ext-configure gd --with-jpeg --with-freetype` für Bildunterstützung

- Heruntergeladenes `.tgz` nach Extraktion löschen

**Beispielstruktur:**
```
FROM php:8.4-apache

LABEL maintainer tim@arctium.io

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    libpng-dev libjpeg-dev libfreetype6-dev libicu-dev \
    && docker-php-ext-configure gd --with-jpeg --with-freetype \
    && docker-php-ext-install -j$(nproc) gd intl mbstring opcache \
    && apt-get purge -y --auto-remove -o APT::AutoRemove::RecommendsImportant=false \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN curl -O https://download.dokuwiki.org/src/dokuwiki/dokuwiki-2025-05-14.tgz \
    && tar -xzf dokuwiki-2025-05-14.tgz --strip-components=1 -C /var/www/html \
    && rm dokuwiki-2025-05-14.tgz \
    && find /var/www/html -type d -exec chmod 755 {} \; \
    && find /var/www/html -type f -exec chmod 644 {} \; \

input.content:
# dokuwiki-docker
Simple to use and highly versatile open-source wiki... conveniently packaged as a container image

> This Dockerfile contains a streamlined and not blown-up approach to run a dockerized version of dokuwiki.
> It's based on the `php:8.4-apache` image which ships with Apache and PHP 8.4 right out of the box.

## How-to use this

Instead of just starting the image, you should consider using a docker-compose file to spin up your services. The example file will attach a persistent volume to your dokuwiki service and make sure the needed ports are opened.

```yaml
services:
  dokuwiki:
    build: .
    ports:
      - '80:80'
      - '443:443'
    volumes:
      - 'data:/var/www/html'
volumes:
  data:
```

Once you either navigated to the cloned repo or created the file by yourself, you can use these commands:

**Start the Service via**

`docker compose up`

**Tear down the Service via**

`docker compose down`
